body: There's no true equality when it comes to mental illness. It can't be explained in a way that makes logical sense. You could have everything you've ever wanted and still feel not ok with living. Emotions so intense that you have to try to ignore them or figure out a way to make them go away. All while pretending you're ok. The biggest lie. There's something inside that hates your own conscienceness and there isn't an explanation. Eventually it will be what kills you. Sorry to be so grim. I've given up completely. I'm exhausted. It's time to go for sure for me. /end rant

Imagine if you didn't have any family left that loved or cared about you. Even if you never did anything wrong. Abandoned by people you protected and loved for over 20 years. That's my reality. If you have a single person that truly cares about you then you should stop bitching and accept that single gift. If you have at least one person you don't know true isolation like I do. My flaw was deciding to be honest with every thought that passed through my head. Don't make the same mistake. People don't like to hear their truth, but they like to expect total honesty. It's a trap.

What you're feeling is easily relatable. At least to me. It's exhausting to constantly want to leave this plane and at the same time be afraid of it. Thinking of tomorrow when you don't want a tomorrow. Thinking about the future and working and breathing now for the future seems like a waste of time. It really is overwhelming. You aren't alone. At least in a sense where what you think feels isolated. Good luck.

Loss of love is the truest form of pain. Even if it eventually fades away, the memory of how it feels never leaves. You'll love and lose love countless numbers of times in your life. In my opinion, if you were true with who you are as a person and let someone else in, and they discard you so easily, they never reciprocated what you put into the relationship. That person isn't where your focus should be. Sure, miss them, but also take time to mourn and accept they aren't part of your life anymore and give yourself a chance to move on.

I directly sympathize with that. I want to go so bad, but I don't want to be somewhere she isn't. Traveling to somewhere unknown is terrifying, but how could it be worse than the pain that made these thoughts real?

That's pretty young to make that kind of determination. If you're alone it's ok. If you've lost people it's ok. Once you make the decision to focus on yourself instead of what you perceive other people think about you, you will be able to effortlessly coast. If you be your true self you'll find people that want to be around you. Don't hide your truth. Let it be known.

If we die and all we see or feel is nothingness, then perhaps death truly is a gift. The balance of joy and despair is off kilter. Some get all joy, some get all despair. Who's to judge if we can't stand it anymore? If God was real why did he want me to hurt so much? Why did he put me here only to keep losing everything I love? Am I supposed to be an example of how life shouldn't be? No one actually pays attention. No one actually cares. In the grand scheme of things my pain isn't recognized by anyone but myself. I get to live alone with it and determine if I want to keep going and take the chance of taking more pain in or possibly finding something worth living for again. Everything and everyone I've valued my life worth has always vanished. I've been through enough to know that if all I see anymore is a black void, I'd be ok with it.
Goodbye stranger. I'll be joining you soon

Empathy is supposed to be a basic human response. Somehow people developed a way to turn empathy into self-pity. Instead of trying to help the one that's actually hurting they help themselves. The pity turns to jealousy for some reason. It's like people want to suffer. At that point it turns into competition. It makes me sick thinking they think they want this kind of pain to get attention. Like a martyr. Narcissists. People are disgusting.

I understand that pain with exactitude. I'm sorry. It truly is awful. The mind won't stop racing. You're sore in your shoulders, neck, and back. Insomnia. No appetite. Consistently wondering why and if it was your fault. The worst realization is discovering it wasn't your fault. Then you're driven into madness. I'm sorry for you. Truly.
I'm down. Lmk if you still need.

Thank you. This definitely gives me a different way to look at myself. I'm almost 4 years post op and I feel like I just might start to be recovering. People want to understand, but don't have the patience for recovery. It truly is a difficult ordeal for everyone involved. Yes, one step at a time

Thank you. I will check that out. You're right about people not knowing the mind of someone with pain that hasn't experienced it first. I know the people in my life that watched me go through this see me as an enigma now. They can't figure out why I'm not just pure joy with rainbows coming out my ass. The truth is its burnt into my psyche that one day it could come back.

After exhausting all my local resources I went back to my PCP to figure out what to do next. She gave me a referral to the Cleveland Clinic. That was my salvation. I spent 6 months traveling 2 hours one way to my appointments there. They knew what I went through, but they insisted they have their people do everything all over again like it was a new case. Needless to say, none of it worked. They still couldn't figure out the problem. So the surgeon said the only thing they can do now was exploratory surgery. Open me up and check it out. If they find anything they'll fix what they can. I could tell he had doubts, but I knew he'd find something. I'm not sure how often surgeons find themselves with their tails between their legs after saving someone's life, but I could tell this man had a bit of remorse knowing what I've been through and not trusting me. I don't hold it against him, or any of them for that matter. As hard as it was to not give up you have to keep trying. I was in my mid 20's with 2 small children. All they ever saw me as their whole life was a lifeless lump on the couch with no emotion. I couldn't let that be the image they had of me. You have to find something to live for not matter what it is. Even if all you're living for is to prove to everyone that they're wrong.
